# Architecture decisions

**Responsibility:** index the architecture decisions and their recorded rationale.  
**Authority:** historical decision record.  
**Owner role:** architecture.
**Change policy:** supersede via a new ADR; do not edit accepted ADRs in place.

Use an ADR when a choice changes an interface, invariant, data model, deployment guarantee, or supported workload. An ADR must state context, decision, alternatives, consequences, evidence, and revisit conditions.

Decisions do not override newer accepted requirements. When a decision is superseded, preserve it and link the replacement.

- [ADR 0001: Repository structure](0001-repository-structure.md) defines the one-package framework and role-folder layout.
- [ADR 0002: Clarify the adopted v4 contracts](0002-v4-contract-clarifications.md) reconciles the final API, transaction, and capability decisions without claiming runtime implementation.
- [ADR 0003: Failure rollback, automatic scoping, drain, and hosted trust](0003-failure-scoping-drain-and-hosted-trust.md) resolves the corresponding open decisions from ADR 0002 and requires context-scoped adapters, without claiming implementation or backend support.
- [ADR 0004: Receipt access, revocation, and command expiry](0004-receipt-access-revocation-and-expiry.md) restricts receipt access, preserves accepted work after revocation, and requires enforceable rejection of expired external command identities.
- [ADR 0005: Turn round trips, turn batches, and regional placement](0005-turn-latency-batching-and-regional-placement.md) limits a turn to two database round trips, lets waiting commands for one actor share a transaction, and places hosted tenants in home regions.
- [ADR 0006: Scale rules, placement keys, and query tiers](0006-scale-rules-placement-and-query-tiers.md) adds per-type placement keys and a framework routing key, enforces single-shard hot paths, defines local/group/fleet query tiers, and prohibits database-wide serialization points. Its bucket-ownership rule for due-work scans is amended by ADR 0021.
- [ADR 0007: Foundation command protocol](0007-foundation-command-protocol.md) specifies the first embedded Postgres identity, authorization, receipt, and transaction implementation and its unsupported boundaries.
- [ADR 0008: Foundation identity, policies, defects, and PGlite](0008-foundation-completion.md) completes M0 identity modes, lifecycle policies, creation gating, bounded turns, deterministic `onDefect` handling, System callers, and the shared PGlite/Postgres test boundary.
- [ADR 0009: Colocated tests and a separate browser project](0009-colocated-tests-and-browser-e2e.md) requires unit and integration tests beside matching source files and places browser E2E in its own workspace.
- [ADR 0010: One way to do everything: the Effect-native actor API](0010-one-way-effect-native-api.md) makes `Actor.make(name, definition)` the only actor shape, adds reducers, delivers context as typed per-phase services, removes layer options, and gives calls one form outside turns and intents one form inside.
- [ADR 0011: Direct commands, one outbox, and the performance architecture](0011-direct-commands-outbox-and-performance.md) makes commands direct with the receipt as their durable record, carries every intent and timer in one actor-shard outbox, pipelines turn batches, and records reducers, read-your-writes queries, compressed and cold state, single durability, operations, and simulation testing (dictionary requirement amended by ADR 0017). Its relay-per-owned-bucket rule is amended by ADR 0021.
- [ADR 0012: Workflow storage, internal commands, effect routes, defects, merging, and home regions](0012-workflows-internals-effects-defects-merging-regions.md) adds a framework `WorkflowEngine` on the owner's shard, an `internal` definition section, declared `onSuccess`/`onDeadLetter` effect routes, telemetry-only defects, never-waiting commutative merges, and operator-assigned home regions.
- [ADR 0013: Reconcile the shipped M0 code with ADRs 0010–0012](0013-m0-reconciliation.md) moves the implemented foundation to the one-object `Actor.make`, input-only handlers with a per-actor `X.Turn`, `X.create()`-only minting, ambient caller and tenant, telemetry-only defects, and direct commands with no Cluster message storage (its "Not implemented" list is corrected by ADR 0017).
- [ADR 0014: Adoption, observation, and client reach](0014-adoption-observation-and-client-reach.md) makes existing Postgres adoption, query observation, offline command replay, workflow compatibility checks, inspection/export, generated protocols, and scale-to-zero runner support the next product differentiators.
- [ADR 0015: Durable agent runtime boundary](0015-durable-agent-runtime-boundary.md) (superseded by ADR 0017) defined an agent runtime as an actor-native control plane with durable business state and replaceable sandbox compute, without making an AI-specific runtime part of the core actor package.
- [ADR 0016: Generated durable applications](0016-generated-durable-applications.md) records dynamic applications as a gated product direction: generate contracts and handlers, validate them, and activate them behind tenant isolation rather than executing arbitrary generated servers by default.
- [ADR 0017: M1 record corrections](0017-m1-record-corrections.md) marks ADR 0013's unimplemented list as stale, supersedes ADR 0015 because Outlast is a separate product, amends state storage to plain zstd with a stored codec version, and accepts `placement: "tenant" | "actor"`.
- [ADR 0018: Benchmark harness and committed results](0018-benchmark-harness-and-results.md) places the `bun run bench` harness in `tooling/benchmarks/` and keeps its immutable, machine-labelled result files in a top-level `benchmarks/` directory.
- [ADR 0019: Runner capacity and Postgres pool size](0019-runner-capacity-and-pool-size.md) makes the runner's activation limit the `maxResidentActors` option, reports reaching it as the typed, retryable `RunnerAtCapacity` instead of `MailboxFull`, and defaults the Postgres pool to 50 connections.
- [ADR 0020: The two-round-trip turn pipeline](0020-two-round-trip-turn-pipeline.md) sends each turn as two pipelined statement groups on a turn-owned multiplexed `@effect/sql-pg` connection, keeps contract 02's order, and rejects the optimistic one-round-trip fast path.
- [ADR 0021: Multi-runner relay, effect executors, singletons, and cron](0021-multi-runner-relay-singleton-and-cron.md) (accepted 2026-09-26) lets every runner claim due outbox rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and a lease instead of owning buckets, moves effect executors to a per-runner pool with renewed leases, makes effect timings policy, backs off rows that die unsettled, keeps post-commit wakes local, and runs cron as keyed self-timers the relay rewrites; it uses `0011_relay`, and cron needs no migration.
- [ADR 0022: Workflow engine storage, runs, owner-event waits, and version markers](0022-workflow-engine-storage-and-version-markers.md) (accepted 2026-09-26) settles the `0012_workflows` schema, execution ids, `WorkflowRun`, the `waitFor` race, activity call identity, retention, typed step constructors, `wf.version`, and the deploy compatibility check.
- [ADR 0026: Cross-actor event subscriptions](0026-cross-actor-event-subscriptions.md) (proposed) delivers committed events to subscriber actors as receipt-deduplicated System command turns through the outbox relay, with fan-out after commit, per-source order, subscriber cursors, bounded retention holds with explicit gaps, and same-tenant scope.
